## Computational growth across warehouse populations

The native Gurobi records separate two changes in the workload. At h215 W,
the move from DET to STO expands the matrix from 1.56 to 14.05 million
variables and from 5.79 to 52.07 million nonzeros, about ninefold in both
cases. The 307 binary variables are shared investment decisions in STO.
With four threads in both observations, native time rises from 2.04 to
40.76 min and sampled application RSS from 5.54 to 43.13 GiB. The attained
gaps are 0.000812% and 0.740159%, respectively. These are observed effort
ratios for different formulations and attained gaps.

Across the W STO series, h215 to h500 increases the number of variables by
4.51 times and matrix nonzeros by 4.69 times. Model build time grows by
4.56 times, native time by 3.13 times and sampled application RSS by 2.59
times. The h215 observation used four threads. The h300, h400 and h500
observations used one. Over this one-thread subset, h300 to h500 increases
variables by 2.53 times, matrix nonzeros by 2.58 times, native time by 2.71
times and RSS by 2.41 times. The h500 incumbent satisfies the target with
an attained gap of 0.207432% after 127.58 min of native time and 152.72 min
end-to-end. The scale-up comparisons use the historical native cohort
in @tbl-scalar-size, @tbl-scalar-resources and @tbl-scalar-quality.

## Fixed-instance scaling and attainment in common Pyomo

All 30 h300 W STO cells returned terminal observations. The two solvers
received the same ordered Pyomo matrix, with 25.11 million variables and
94.97 million nonzeros. The comparison uses three temporal repetitions
per solver and thread ceiling, the common 1% relative-gap target and
an eight-hour native time limit. @tbl-h300-repeated summarizes the
median terminal clocks and the count of independently validated
incumbents meeting the target. Appendix C reports the full ranges, gaps
and sampled worker-tree memory.

| Threads | Gurobi at target | Gurobi native / end-to-end, min | HiGHS at target | HiGHS native / end-to-end, min |
|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| 1 | 3/3 | 48.23 / 91.97 | 3/3 | 401.43 / 443.35 |
| 2 | 3/3 | 66.18 / 108.94 | 0/3 | 480.79 / 513.14 |
| 4 | 3/3 | 65.14 / 113.14 | 0/3 | 480.61 / 513.04 |
| 8 | 3/3 | 93.29 / 136.00 | 0/3 | 480.62 / 513.16 |
| 16 | 3/3 | 96.39 / 141.15 | 0/3 | 480.60 / 512.78 |

: Common-Pyomo h300 W STO attainment and median times to termination. HiGHS medians at 2–16 threads describe time-limit returns without a usable incumbent. {#tbl-h300-repeated}

At one thread, the HiGHS-to-Gurobi ratio of median terminal time is
8.32 for the native clock and 4.82 end-to-end. The respective
attained gaps are 0.006879% and 0.004105%. At the other four settings,
all 12 HiGHS repetitions reached the limit without a usable incumbent.
For these cells the time to a validated target is unobserved and the
incumbent-based gaps are unavailable. Native times slightly above
480 min are observed terminal readings under the configured budget.

All Gurobi runs reached the target, with attained gaps between 0.004105%
and 0.004122%. @tbl-h300-scaling gives the strong-scaling indicators for
the fixed problem under this stopping policy. They use the median of
three runs per ceiling and the corresponding one-thread median. Efficiency
is normalized by the solver thread ceiling. The observed clocks measure
termination; the time of first reaching the target was not recorded.

| Threads | Native speedup | Native efficiency, % | End-to-end speedup | End-to-end efficiency, % |
|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| 1 | 1.000 | 100.0 | 1.000 | 100.0 |
| 2 | 0.729 | 36.4 | 0.844 | 42.2 |
| 4 | 0.740 | 18.5 | 0.813 | 20.3 |
| 8 | 0.517 | 6.5 | 0.676 | 8.5 |
| 16 | 0.500 | 3.1 | 0.652 | 4.1 |

: Descriptive Gurobi h300 strong-scaling indicators based on median terminal times under the shared stopping policy. {#tbl-h300-scaling}

Each multithreaded Gurobi setting takes longer than the one-thread
setting on both median clocks. At 16 threads the median native time
is approximately double and the end-to-end time is 1.53 times the
one-thread value. The sampled worker-tree peak rises from 74.42 GiB
at one thread to 100.88 GiB at 16. At two and four threads the
native-time ranges overlap the one-thread range. At eight and
sixteen threads they lie entirely above it in the three observed
repetitions. The per-setting ranges characterize this run block.

## Evidence at h400 and coverage of h500

The h400 common-Pyomo matrix contains 42.11 million variables and
161.25 million nonzeros, compared with 25.11 million and 94.97 million
at h300. The E1 and E2 follow-up runs complete one observation per
solver and thread ceiling at h400 W STO. The ten receipts bind the
same inputs, ordered matrix, bounds and hardware class to the 192 GiB
profile and eight-hour native budget. E1 supplies one and sixteen
threads, and E2 supplies two, four and eight. Appendix C distinguishes
these observations from the original h400 pilots.

Gurobi reached the 1% target in all five configurations. Each returned
the same reported penalized objective, BRL 7.593395 trillion, and
economic subtotal, BRL 381.573 billion. The attained gaps agree to six
decimal places at 0.836784%. HiGHS reached the time limit without a
usable incumbent at every thread ceiling. Its native terminal times
range from 481.13 to 481.39 min. Its incumbent objectives and gaps are
unavailable. @tbl-h400-followup reports both terminal clocks and
Gurobi's descriptive speedup relative to the E1 one-thread observation.

| Threads | Gurobi native / end-to-end, min | Gurobi native / end-to-end speedup | HiGHS native / end-to-end, min |
|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| 1 | 87.36 / 162.60 | 1.000 / 1.000 | 481.13 / 534.88 |
| 2 | 80.03 / 154.83 | 1.092 / 1.050 | 481.39 / 535.59 |
| 4 | 139.63 / 214.98 | 0.626 / 0.756 | 481.35 / 536.08 |
| 8 | 150.36 / 226.35 | 0.581 / 0.718 | 481.37 / 536.96 |
| 16 | 134.60 / 207.78 | 0.649 / 0.783 | 481.28 / 534.81 |

: h400 W STO terminal clocks and Gurobi speedup in the E1–E2 follow-up. All Gurobi runs reached the target. All HiGHS times describe censoring without a usable incumbent. Each setting has one observation. {#tbl-h400-followup}

The two-thread Gurobi run had the lowest observed time on both clocks,
with nominal efficiencies of 54.6% native and 52.5% end-to-end.
Its sampled worker-tree peak was 133.13 GiB compared with 113.31 GiB
at one thread. Across both solvers the largest sampled worker-tree
and job-cgroup peaks were 162.99 and 163.45 GiB, respectively, both
from Gurobi at sixteen threads. Both were within the follow-up gate
limits. Appendix C reports the two memory measurements for each cell.

The original 90-cell campaign remains a separate record. It retained
20 validated target attainments and 14 observations without usable
incumbents. The remaining 56 cells, including 26 at h400 and all 30
at h500, were cancelled before execution. The native h500 solution
remains the largest validated instance in the reported series.
